grounding_spans.text: When a WHERE clause is present, SQLite evaluates its expression for each input row and filters the input before result rows are produced. If a SELECT returns multiple rows without ORDER BY, SQLite does not define the order in which those rows are returned. An ORDER BY clause determines result-row ordering from its expressions; ASC orders smaller values first and DESC orders larger values first. When multiple ORDER BY expressions are present, SQLite sorts by the left-most expression first and uses later expressions to break ties.

lessons.objective: Use SELECT for the requested columns and WHERE for row-level conditions.
lessons.title: Choose columns, then filter rows

grounding_spans.text: If a SELECT returns multiple rows without ORDER BY, SQLite does not define the order in which those rows are returned. An ORDER BY clause determines result-row ordering from its expressions; ASC orders smaller values first and DESC orders larger values first. When multiple ORDER BY expressions are present, SQLite sorts by the left-most expression first and uses later expressions to break ties.
`SELECT title, priority FROM tasks WHERE done = 0 ORDER BY priority DESC, title ASC` sorts incomplete tasks by highest priority first and alphabetically within a priority tie.
`SELECT owner, title FROM tasks WHERE priority >= 2 ORDER BY owner ASC, title ASC` sorts qualifying tasks by owner and then title.
